title: Response Token Dissector — wireframes & playbook
body:
Overview:

This is a working draft for a compact, explorable panel in the Console called the "Response Token Dissector" (RTD). Goal: give developers a token-level breakdown that combines cost attribution, micro-latency, and source provenance (prompt vs cached KV vs model expansion) in a single, tileable UI that can be dropped into Invocation Detail, Trace Explorer, or a dedicated Token Forensics view.

Design principles / constraints:
- Always-scalable: supports short responses (10 tokens) to long streamed responses (2k+ tokens) without freezing the page.
- Low cognitive overhead: default to an aggregated view, allow progressive disclosure to token-level detail.
- Actionable: each token slice should offer quick actions (pin span, copy prompt slice, mark as noisy, create eval pair).
- Correlatable: link tokens to cost units (microcosts), KV hits, batching decisions, and model variant fallbacks.
- Lightweight rendering: use canvas/webgl sparklines for microtimings to avoid 2k DOM nodes.

Primary views (wireframe states):

1) Compact row (default)
- Left: small invocation header (model, route, time, total tokens, total cost)
- Middle: token-timeline mini-sparkline (scrollable horizontally). Each token is a narrow column with stacked microbars: compute ms, IO ms, KV hit flag, quantization flag. Color legend above. Hover shows tooltip with token text, token index, per-token token-cost (USD), latency breakdown, and likely source (prompt / kv-cache / fallback).
- Right: quick-actions menu (pin, open full dissect, create ticket, mark for eval)

2) Expanded pane (slide-over)
- Top row: full response text with inline token selection mode (shift+click to select spans). Selected spans highlight corresponding columns in the timeline below.
- Middle: expanded timeline with grouped aggregates (by 1/5/10 token bins) and ability to toggle grouping. Each column shows: token-cost, compute-ms, io-ms, batch-size-at-gen, host-id.
- Bottom: attribution table (sortable) with rows: token-range, cost-contrib, p95-latency, kv-hit-rate, batch-size, model-variant. Actions column for each row.
- Side rail: quick diagnosis checklist autogenerated (heuristics) — e.g., "High per-token compute, check quantization profile" or "KV miss spike near tokens 120–135, likely due to prefix mismatch". Buttons: suggest cache-keys, propose partial re-run with reduced context.

3) Forensics mode (full-screen)
- Timeline scrubber synced with overall trace (open tracing span links). Selecting a token range will show associated request headers, route config, batching group id, and GPU host kernel selection at time-of-generation. Includes a "replay chunk" control that will re-run the selected span against a sandboxed model variant (DEV only).

Heuristics & attribution notes (implementation-facing):
- Per-token cost = model-cost-per-token * token-length-factor + infra-surcharge * (gpu-ms / avg-ms). We should store both raw token-charge (billing) and an internal microcost so the UI can explain differences (e.g., billing rounds differently).
- Latency slices: we split per-token latency into 3 buckets: input-io (serialize / network to runtime), compute (attention + FFN + kernel overhead), and output-io (token marshalling + network back). Each column shows absolute ms and % of token time.
- KV tagging: token provenance detection uses three signals: exact KV key hit, prefix-KV fuzzy match score (>0.92), and prefix-length ratio. Provide confidence score in tooltip.
- Batching inference: we attach the observed batch-size that token belonged to. Where possible, infer if the token benefited from batch-joining (higher throughput) or was isolated (latency-sensitive).

Wireframe annotations / micro-interactions:
- Hovering a token: fast tooltip with two actionable links: "open full trace" and "open prompt context". Tooltip includes small sparkline of last 10 token latencies.
- Select span: top-of-pane contextual actions: "compare span to golden prompt", "add to regression set", "propose quant profile change".
- Pin token/span: pins to the top of invocation list in the Console (persist across sessions for the user). Pinned items show a subtle badge and are available in a separate "Pinned Forensics" workspace.
- Keyboard: / toggles token-selection mode, left/right to jump tokens, g to group 10 tokens, shift+P to pin.

Accessibility notes:
- Token bars must have accessible labels (token index, text preview, ms breakdown) presented to screen readers in the expanded view.
- Heatmap colors should have a high-contrast alternate palette for colorblind users; allow user preference in settings.

Backlog & engineering tickets (draft):
- UX-1291: RTD minimal prototype (compact row + hover tooltip) — MVP.
- PROD-842: Instrument per-token microtimings in runtime (input-io, compute, output-io) and expose in trace payload.
- INF-501: Add batch-size attribution to token events in the runtime telemetry (includes host-id and kernel tag).
- DX-333: Sandbox replay service for span replays (DEV-only, gated).
- DATA-77: Store per-token KV confidence and provide sampling endpoint for large invocations.

Sample user stories / acceptance criteria:
- As an SRE, I can open Invocation Detail and see the RTD compact row for any completed invocation; hover reveals per-token tooltip and I can pin a noisy token to my workspace.
- As an ML engineer, I can select a 10-token span and add it to a regression prompt set with one click.
- As a Platform engineer, I can correlate high per-token compute with model variant rollouts and use the forensics mode to find a rollback candidate.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- Storage cost vs fidelity: storing full per-token microtimings for every invocation is expensive. Proposal: sample 5% of invocations for full fidelity, store aggregates for all, and allow on-demand re-run to rehydrate missing details. Trade: re-run might not reproduce host-level kernel tags.
- Real-time vs post-hoc: for streaming responses we can render heuristics real-time (approx) but fill in exact microtimings after invocation completes. UI should mark approximations clearly.
- Pinning UX: pins are useful but may proliferate. Need soft limits (50 per user) and TTL (90 days) or allow tagging for org-level shared pins.

Prototype notes (what I sketched during the session):
- Canvas timeline with layered bars: bottom layer = compute-ms (blue), middle = IO-ms (orange), thin top stripe = kv-hit (green) when present. Token width adapts; show an approximate count marker every 50 tokens.
- Expanded table: lazy-render using virtualized rows. Grouping toggle with presets: 1,5,10,50, adaptive.
- Small reveal: dropping a tiny "cost microledger" modal from any token that summarizes the billable tokens, internal microcost, and a link to "why they differ" doc.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally names a few backend telemetry fields to ensure clear scoping. Please flag any fields that are impossible/unavailable today (e.g., kernel tag at token granularity).
- We should prioritize the compact row MVP first (low UI complexity + big diagnostic win). Prototype plan: 2-week spike to produce a React + canvas prototype that hooks to a synthetic trace endpoint.

Immediate next steps:
- Ravi: confirm instrumentation feasibility with serving-runtime (PROD-842) and estimate cost for sampling vs full persistence.
- Elena: draft high-fidelity compact-row mockups and hand off to front-end for the spike.
- Samir: write the acceptance tests for "pin/ add to regression set / open trace" flows.
- Ava: coordinate a 45-minute review with Console PMs + SRE next Thursday; create meeting notes and circulate.

Appendix — quick backlog notionals (phrases to convert into tickets):
- "approx token microcost API"
- "kv-confidence score export"
- "token-pin TTL and sharing model"
- "replay sandbox auth gating"

End of draft.

(Informal notes: I was short on time during the sketch session so some wireframe spacing/annotation is messy — expect the first mockups to be rough. Comments inline preferred over rewrite — I want to capture the raw heuristics here.)
